title: {name} Public Sector
description: AI for everyone in a local government or public body: Albert, GWDG’s SAIA or your own AI, through your gateway. Open source, with no server of ours.
eyebrow: For local governments, ministries and public bodies
h1: AI for all your staff, under your rules.
lede: {name} is a folder of static files your IT serves from your administration’s own address. It answers only through your AI gateway, to a public service such as Albert, a shared provider or your own servers, and people sign in with their work account. No server of ours, nothing to install, no price per seat.
nokey: Nobody needs a key to use {name}.
nokey.why: A key is only for a public body that hosts its own {name}, for the audit export, retention and long-term support releases.
ai.title: Which AI for local government? The one you govern.
ai.why: {name} gives all your staff a way into the AI your policy names, and no other. Each person signs in with their work account, which your gateway takes as its key.

answers.security: Only those your policy names: Albert, GWDG’s SAIA, a shared provider or your own servers, behind your gateway.
With your identity provider, over OpenID Connect. Their sign-in goes to your gateway as its key.
On their own computer, sealed with AES-256-GCM. They go only to your gateway and what your policy allows, never to our servers.
Its 35 recommendations for generative AI systems are mapped one by one in the trust pack: what {name} does, what is left to you, what isn’t built.
{name} is a static folder any host can serve. Where your needs call for it, what counts is where the gateway and the AI run, and your policy names only those.
Has it been tested from outside?
The brief for the test is published. The test isn’t done yet.
answers.purchasing: MIT, for everything people use. The audit export and retention are under Elastic 2.0 with a key, and become MIT if no key can be bought for 12 months.
Everything is plain files and open standards, and nothing sits on our servers.
For WCAG 2.2 AA, what EN 301 549 asks of web content. It says “partially conformant” and lists what isn’t yet. Yours can build on it.
The checks are Warehouse SAS’s own, by automated tests and by hand. No outside audit has been done yet.

mail.subject: An AI for all our staff, for review
mail.body:
Hello,

Here is an AI we could deploy for all our staff. It would answer only through our gateway, with our own accounts, and with no server at the vendor’s. Each question of the review has its answer there, with its status today:

{page}

Could you read it before we talk it over?
